lesson.title: ¿Cuánto Cuesta? Prices and Play Money to Cien
lesson.subject: spanish

contentBlocks.text: You've counted, listened, and played a guessing game with numbers to cien. Today your numbers go shopping: you'll ask how much something costs, and count out play money all the way to one hundred.

To ask a price in Spanish, say ¿Cuánto cuesta? — 'How much does it cost?' The answer starts with cuesta ('it costs') and then the number: Cuesta cuarenta dólares. Cuesta noventa y cinco centavos. The number word works exactly the way you learned it this week — tens word, then y, then the ones.

Counting money is really just the tens chant with a job to do. Line up play bills of ten and count them out loud:

diez, veinte, treinta, cuarenta, cincuenta, sesenta, setenta, ochenta, noventa, cien

Now mix in a five or some ones to land on an in-between price. Four tens and a five is cuarenta y cinco. Seven tens and three ones is setenta y tres. Practice counting a small pile of play money out loud, naming the new total in Spanish each time you add a bill.

Prices aren't the only place big numbers show up at a store. Quantities do too:

¿Cuántos hay? (How many are there?)
Hay cincuenta manzanas. (There are fifty apples.)

Count something real in big groups — a box of crayons, a bag of beans, the pages in a short book — and say the total in Spanish.

You just used this week's numbers for two real jobs: asking a price and counting money to cien. Tomorrow you'll pull the whole week together in one fast game — a hundred-chart challenge covering every number to cien.

items.prompt: Escribe el número: '¿Cuánto cuesta? Cuesta cuarenta.'
Escribe el número: 'Cuesta sesenta y cinco.'
Escribe el número: 'Cuesta ochenta y dos.'

objectives: Ask a price with ¿Cuánto cuesta? and understand an answer of the form Cuesta + number
Count play money to cien by tens, then adjust to an in-between total with fives and ones
Ask and answer ¿Cuántos hay? with a number in the 40-100 range
materialsNeeded: Play money (paper bills of 10, plus a few 5s and 1s), or slips of paper labeled with amounts
A family member to shop and count with
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Ask the child how they'd ask a price in English, then introduce ¿Cuánto cuesta? and the answer frame Cuesta + number.
2. Count a stack of ten play bills together out loud: diez, veinte, treinta... cien.
3. Add a five and some ones to make in-between prices (cuarenta y cinco, setenta y tres); have the child name each new total in Spanish.
4. Introduce ¿Cuántos hay? and answer with Hay + number, counting a real group of objects.
5. Set up a tiny store: price three or four objects with paper tags, then take turns asking ¿Cuánto cuesta? and paying with play money.
6. Complete the translate activity.
7. Complete the worksheet.
8. Preview tomorrow's hundred-chart challenge.
differentiationTips: Struggling: keep every price on a tens number (cuarenta, cincuenta, sesenta...) so counting the play money is a straight tens chant with no adjusting
Ready for more: give exact change — if something costs setenta y cinco and they pay with a hundred, have them count the change back up in Spanish (ochenta, noventa, cien)

This lesson's shopping and counting work as live spoken exchanges with a family member, so they don't depend on the audio-recording gap noted elsewhere this week (open decision, expansion-plan-2026-09.md §12.9)
teacherGuide.answerKey: ¿Cuánto cuesta? = 'how much does it cost?'; the answer is Cuesta + a number (Cuesta cuarenta dólares). Counting ten-bills is the tens chant: diez, veinte, treinta... cien. In-between totals use tens + y + ones: four tens and a five = cuarenta y cinco (45); seven tens and three ones = setenta y tres (73). ¿Cuántos hay? = 'how many are there?', answered with Hay + a number (Hay cincuenta manzanas).
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Puts the week's numbers to an authentic interpretive-listening use (WA-WL-2015.1.2): understanding a spoken price or quantity is exactly the real-world listening the standard targets, and it is the Day 4 activity the scope-and-sequence names (prices and quantities with play money to 100). Counting money by tens also reinforces the Day 1 chant with a concrete manipulative, the kind of recycling the course's band notes build in.

generationData.instructions: Answer each question about prices and counting to cien.

rows.problem: Something costs 70 dollars. Write the answer in Spanish words: 'Cuesta ___.'
You count play bills of ten: diez, veinte, treinta... Write the next four words in the chant.
You have seven ten-bills and four ones. Write the total in Spanish words.
